record.title: ONS survey reports AI use among UK businesses in September 2026
record.summary: The UK Office for National Statistics reports that 30% of businesses said they used at least one AI technology in September 2026 in Wave 165 of its Business Insights and Conditions Survey. The voluntary survey had 9,933 responses from 38,592 sampled businesses and remains official statistics in development. This is a self-reported adoption estimate; it does not measure productivity, causal impact, or economy-wide effects. The multi-year trend and large-business subgroup are excluded from this account because comparability was not reconciled and the bulletin gives conflicting subgroup thresholds.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: ONS reports that 30% of businesses said they used at least one AI technology in September 2026, based on Wave 165 of its Business Insights and Conditions Survey. This is an ONS-reported survey estimate, not a causal or productivity result.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: ONS states that Wave 165 ran from 21 September to 4 October 2026, sampled 38,592 businesses and received 9,933 responses (25.7%); the bulletin identifies the statistics as official statistics in development.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The survey estimate does not establish productivity gains, causal economic impact, or AI use across every UK business; the multi-year trend and large-business subgroup are not assessed in this record.

evidence_gaps.description: The Wave 165 confidence-interval workbook gives intervals for individual AI technology responses, but its All businesses row does not provide an interval for the bulletin’s composite “at least one AI technology” estimate. The composite confidence interval is therefore not reported here.

The bulletin gives conflicting employee thresholds for its large-business subgroup; the subgroup is excluded. The reported multi-year trend is also excluded because comparability around question changes was not reconciled.

brief.importance_rationale: If representative of the covered business population, a national adoption estimate can inform public understanding and policy monitoring of AI diffusion. The consequence is moderate because it is a self-reported survey statistic in development, with voluntary response and no measured productivity or causal impact.
limitations: The 30% figure is self-reported survey usage for September 2026, not measured productivity, economic impact or causal effect.
Wave 165 had a 25.7% response rate; responses are voluntary, and ONS classifies these figures as official statistics in development.
The bulletin conflicts on the employee threshold for the large-business subgroup; that subgroup is not included.

No confidence interval for the composite “at least one AI technology” estimate is present in the inspected Wave 165 aggregate workbook; its individual category intervals cannot be combined because responses may overlap.

technical.claimed_result: ONS reports that 30% of businesses said they used at least one AI technology in September 2026, as a Wave 165 survey estimate.
technical.demonstrated_result: The release and questionnaire document the estimate’s survey source and scope; they do not establish independent measurement of adoption, productivity or causal impact.
technical.mechanism: Voluntary business survey asking respondents to self-report current use of at least one listed AI technology.
technical.regime: UK BICS Wave 165, fielded 21 September–4 October 2026; respondents among 38,592 sampled businesses.
technical.strongest_baseline: No matched baseline claimed in this record.

brief.title: ONS survey reports AI use among UK businesses in September 2026
brief.why_it_matters: A nationally reported survey estimate offers a useful indicator of business AI adoption for policy and economic monitoring. Its meaning is limited by voluntary response, developing-statistics status and unresolved uncertainty; adoption is not evidence of productivity or causal economic impact.
